books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

stimulus.source_note: Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, February 2, 1848, Articles V and XII (ratified text). Public domain.
stimulus.text:
Article V. The boundary line between the two Republics shall commence in the Gulf of Mexico, three leagues from land, opposite the mouth of the Rio Grande, otherwise called Rio Bravo del Norte . . . from thence up the middle of that river, following the deepest channel, where it has more than one, to the point where it strikes the southern boundary of New Mexico . . . The southern and western limits of New Mexico, mentioned in the article, are those laid down in the map entitled "Map of the United Mexican States, as organized and defined by various acts of the Congress of said republic, and constructed according to the best authorities. Revised edition. Published at New York, in 1847, by J. Disturnell," of which map a copy is added to this treaty, bearing the signatures and seals of the undersigned Plenipotentiaries.

Article XII. In consideration of the extension acquired by the boundaries of the United States, as defined in the fifth article of the present treaty, the Government of the United States engages to pay to that of the Mexican Republic the sum of fifteen millions of dollars.

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: The treaty's payment of $15 million is best understood as which of the following?

options.text: The price the United States paid Mexico for California and the Southwest, the Mexican Cession.
A fine Mexico paid the United States for starting the war.
options.misconception: The money flowed the other way: the United States paid Mexico, not the reverse.

options.text: The cost of building a railroad across the land bought in the Gadsden Purchase.
options.misconception: The Gadsden Purchase was a separate deal in 1853, for $10 million and a strip south of the Gila.

options.text: Repayment of the debts American citizens claimed Mexico owed them.
options.misconception: The United States did assume some claims against Mexico, but the $15 million in Article XII was the price of the land.

rationales.A: Article XII ties the $15 million to the extension of the boundaries — the land the United States gained.
rationales.B: Mexico received the money; it did not pay a fine to the United States.
rationales.C: The Gadsden Purchase came five years later and cost $10 million, not $15 million.
rationales.D: Claims against Mexico were handled in separate articles; the $15 million was the land payment.
rationales.general:
1. Read Article XII. The $15 million is “in consideration of the extension” of the boundaries.
2. Ask what the United States got for it: California, Nevada, Utah, and parts of four more present-day states.
3. See the bargain. A war won on the battlefield still ended with a purchase, which let the United States call the land bought, not just taken.
Remember: the price tag tells you the deal — $15 million bought the Southwest, and the payment made conquest look like a sale.
